module: Posthoc source-numeral coverage diagnostic, separate from the 100-query paired sample
registration: Written after the original 100-query automatic analysis revealed no eligible numeral cases, but before this analyst examined any responses from this new diagnostic module.
selection: All frozen test records whose original source contains a Python Unicode decimal digit (regex \d); apply the existing seed-2026 hash order and one-record-per-connected-group rule. The available test file contains exactly 10 such records in 10 groups.
invariants: No change to original 100-query plan or its outputs
Identical generation settings, prompt policy, embedding artifacts and training pool as the main study
Freeze a separate runner and plan before module generation
analysis: Reuse independently verified source/reference lexical and length diagnostics, but report numeral flags as primary module description. For each model and condition, denominator is 10 digit-containing source records; report matching and differing digit-expression multisets, changed/added/deleted expressions, source/output text, query and group IDs, and raw-response identity. No bootstrap or population estimate is claimed for this exhaustively selected small diagnostic set.
digit_definition: After the original registered normalization, count digit expressions matching \d+(?:[٫.,:/]\d+)*. Number words are not converted; representation changes can be benign and matching tokens can still have wrong units or relations.
interpretation: Numeral-token mismatch is a review flag, not a factual-error judgment. Exact token matching is not proof of preserved meaning. These ten targeted cases do not estimate broad numerical correctness or human naturalness.
